about: The class: a restart finds tmp/<id>.old, a file a replace set aside before it stopped, and the sweep must decide what to do with it before it clears tmp/. Members come from three producers: a replace that stopped at each of its three crash points, an ordinary host fault at restart (something blocks or holds the file in place, or the database cannot be read), and leftovers that describe nothing. One invariant covers every row: when the row exists and either copy holds the bytes it describes, then after Open one of the two paths still holds them, whether Open succeeded or refused. A set-aside file is deleted only when it is provably not needed: the row has no such report, the committed file is in place, or its bytes are not the row's. Anything else is kept and Open refuses to start, naming it, so the next start can try again.

state_words.cur: the file in place, reports/<id>.html: absent | row-bytes | other-bytes | directory (non-empty) | empty-directory | held-open (other-bytes, handle held while Open runs; Windows only)
state_words.old: the set-aside file, tmp/<id>.old: absent | row-bytes | other-bytes | directory (non-empty)
state_words.row: present = a report with row-bytes was saved and gets id 1; none = nothing is stored and the files carry id 7
state_words.db: up | down (the database handle is closed when Open runs)

unplantable_exits.old-gone: the set-aside file vanishes between listing tmp/ and reading it; a race, not a state that can be planted
unplantable_exits.old-unreadable: Lstat or the read of the set-aside file fails for a reason other than not-exist (permissions, a sharing violation); there is no portable way to plant it
